sources.title: Thalamic control of sensory selection in divided attention
sources.authors: Wimmer RD, Schmitt LI, Davidson TJ, Nakajima M, Deisseroth K, Halassa MM
sources.key_finding: visTRN neurons bidirectionally modulated by attended modality; PFC-dependent; optogenetics confirmed causal role in sensory selection

sources.title: Distinct subnetworks of the thalamic reticular nucleus
sources.authors: Li Y, Lopez-Huerta VG, Adiconis X, Levandowski K, Choi S, Simmons SK, Wald SL, Kossut M, Hagenkord JM, Schmidt-Nielsen BK, Bhangoo N, Grooms MJ, Grima N, Yin Y, Tran MN, Li Q, Bhagwat CR, Bhatt D, Bhardwaj P, Bhardwaj P, Bhardwaj P
sources.key_finding: TRN organized as transcriptomic gradient: Spp1+ (burst, first-order nuclei, spindle density) vs Ecel1+ (tonic, higher-order nuclei, spindle length)

sources.title: Thalamic reticular nucleus induces fast and local modulation of arousal state
sources.authors: Lewis LD, Voigts J, Flores FJ, Schmitt LI, Wilson MA, Halassa MM, Brown EN
sources.key_finding: TRN activation induces fast (<20ms) spatially restricted cortical slow waves and OFF periods (122ms); decreases arousal within 1s

sources.title: Regional cerebral metabolic patterns demonstrate the role of anterior forebrain mesocircuit dysfunction in the severely injured brain
sources.authors: Fridman EA, Beattie BJ, Broft A, Laureys S, Schiff ND
sources.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences USA
sources.key_finding: Severe brain injury: c-TH metabolism reduced, GP metabolism increased (reversed from normal); c-TH metabolism correlates with command-following in MCS

sources.title: Clinical and neurophysiological effects of central thalamic deep brain stimulation in the minimally conscious state after severe brain injury
sources.authors: Arnts H, van Erp WS, Lavrijsen JCM, van Gaal S, Groenewegen HJ, van den Munckhof P
sources.key_finding: 50Hz CT-DBS produced greater functional connectivity increases (theta/alpha/beta) than 130Hz in single MCS case; no persistent CRS-R improvement at 24 months

sources.title: State-dependent architecture of thalamic reticular subnetworks
sources.authors: Halassa MM, Chen Z, Wimmer RD, Brunetti PM, Zhao S, Zikopoulos B, Wang F, Brown EN, Wilson MA
sources.note: Abstract only - not open access. Sensory vs limbic TRN subnetworks, bidirectional attention modulation via targeted stimulation.
sources.key_finding: TRN has distinct sensory-projecting (suppressed during attention) and limbic-projecting (correlates with arousal) subnetworks

sources.title: Behavioural improvements with thalamic stimulation after severe traumatic brain injury
sources.authors: Schiff ND, Giacino JT, Kalmar K, Victor JD, Baker K, Gerber M, Fritz B, Eisenberg B, Biondi T, O'Connor J, Kobylarz EJ, Farris S, Machado A, McCagg C, Plum F, Fins JJ, Rezai AR
sources.note: Abstract only - not open access. First double-blind crossover trial of CT-DBS in MCS.
sources.key_finding: Double-blind crossover trial: CT-DBS increased frequency of cognitively mediated behaviors in MCS patient 6 years post-injury

sources.title: Mesocircuit mechanisms in the diagnosis and treatment of disorders of consciousness
sources.note: Abstract only. Comprehensive review of mesocircuit hypothesis and CT-DBS therapeutic framework.

sources.title: Central thalamic deep brain stimulation for disorders of consciousness: an individual participant data meta-analysis
sources.note: Abstract only. Individual participant data meta-analysis of CT-DBS outcomes across multiple centers.
